key_insight: Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators replace flow-based constraints with autoregressive modeling to generate equilibrium molecular samples more expressively and efficiently.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable path for molecular simulation and protein/peptide design by improving sampling quality while retaining exact likelihood-based training and importance-sampling correction.
method: Use an autoregressive generative model instead of a normalizing flow.
Enable sequential inference-time interventions and avoid flow topological constraints.
Train a transferable 132M-parameter model (Robin) within the ArBG framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over flow-based baselines across benchmarks, with especially strong improvements on larger peptide systems like 10-residue Chignolin and over 60% lower zero-shot energy error on 8-residue systems.
watch_item: Autoregressive models may improve flexibility, but practical performance can still depend on sampling order, calibration of importance weights, and compute cost for large molecular systems.
